commands.name: View network configuration
commands.summary: Shows every network adapter with its IP address, DNS servers, gateway and MAC address.

details.whenToUse: Checking which IP address or DNS server you are using, or finding an adapter's MAC address.

syntaxParts.meaning: Windows IP configuration utility.
Full details for every adapter, including disconnected ones.

details.expectedOutput: One block per adapter: description, physical (MAC) address, DHCP status, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, subnet mask, default gateway and DNS servers.

commands.name: Flush the DNS cache
commands.summary: Clears the list of recently looked-up website addresses so Windows asks the DNS server again.

details.whenToUse: A website moved or was fixed but your PC still goes to the old address, or names fail to resolve after a network change.

syntaxParts.meaning: Empty the DNS client resolver cache.

details.expectedOutput: "Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache."
sideEffects: The cache refills automatically. The next visit to each site needs one fresh DNS lookup.

commands.name: Check network connectivity
commands.summary: Sends a few echo requests to a host and reports whether it answers and how fast.

details.whenToUse: You suspect the internet or a specific server is unreachable or slow.

syntaxParts.meaning: Sends ICMP echo requests (4 by default on Windows).
The host name or IP address to test. Replace it with any host.

details.expectedOutput: One "Reply from …" line per request with the round-trip time, then a summary of packet loss and min/max/average times.
cautions: Some servers block ping. No reply does not always mean the host is down.

commands.name: Trace the route to a host
commands.summary: Lists each network hop between this PC and a host, to find where a connection slows down or stops.

details.expectedOutput: Numbered hops with three response times each and the router name or address. "Request timed out" lines are common for routers that don't answer.
cautions: Can take up to a minute or more with many hops.

commands.name: Look up a domain's IP address
commands.summary: Asks your DNS server which IP address a domain name points to.
tasks: what ip does a website have

details.expectedOutput: The DNS server that answered, then the name and its addresses. "Non-authoritative answer" is normal.
cautions: Running nslookup with no arguments starts an interactive mode; type exit to leave it.

commands.name: View active network connections
commands.summary: Lists open connections and listening ports with the process ID that owns each.
tasks: which program is using a port

details.whenToUse: Finding which program is using a port, or checking for unexpected connections.

syntaxParts.meaning: All connections and listening ports.
Numeric addresses and ports (faster, no name lookups).
Show the owning process ID (PID). Match it in Task Manager or tasklist.

details.expectedOutput: Columns: Proto, Local Address, Foreign Address, State, PID.

commands.name: View connections with program names
commands.summary: Like netstat -ano, but shows the executable name behind each connection.
tasks: which program is using a port
which app is connecting to the internet

syntaxParts.meaning: Show the executable involved in each connection.

details.expectedOutput: Each connection followed by the program name in square brackets.
cautions: Requires administrator rights. A standard user gets "The requested operation requires elevation".
Can be slow on busy systems.

commands.name: Show MAC addresses
commands.summary: Lists the physical (MAC) address of each network adapter with the adapter's name.

syntaxParts.meaning: Verbose: include connection name and adapter name.

details.expectedOutput: Columns: Connection Name, Network Adapter, Physical Address, Transport Name.

commands.name: List saved Wi-Fi networks
commands.summary: Shows the Wi-Fi networks this PC has saved profiles for.

details.expectedOutput: "User profiles" followed by one "All User Profile : <name>" line per saved network.
cautions: Shows nothing useful on PCs without a wireless adapter or with the WLAN service stopped.

commands.name: Reset the network stack (Winsock)
commands.summary: Restores the Windows Sockets catalog to its default state. A classic fix for broken internet after malware or VPN software.

details.whenToUse: Internet is broken even though the adapter is connected, and simpler fixes (flushing DNS, restarting the router) didn't help.
details.expectedOutput: "Successfully reset the Winsock Catalog. You must restart the computer in order to complete the reset."
sideEffects: Removes third-party Winsock providers (some VPN, proxy or security software may need reinstalling).

commands.name: List files and directories
commands.summary: Lists the files and folders in the current directory.
tasks: see what is in this folder

details.expectedOutput: Name, size and modified date of each item, plus file and folder totals and free space.

commands.name: Find files by name
commands.summary: Searches the current folder and every subfolder for files matching a pattern, printing full paths.

placeholders.name: Pattern
placeholders.description: File name or wildcard, e.g. *.log or report*.docx

syntaxParts.meaning: Include every subdirectory.
Bare format: full paths only.
What to look for. * matches any characters.

details.expectedOutput: One full path per match, or "File Not Found".
cautions: Starting from C:\ searches the whole drive and can take a long time.

commands.name: Show a folder tree
commands.summary: Draws the folder structure under the current directory, including file names.

syntaxParts.meaning: Include the files in each folder, not just folders.

cautions: Large folders produce very long output.

commands.name: Copy a folder with subfolders
commands.summary: Copies a folder and everything inside it, resuming reliably and reporting what was copied.

placeholders.name: Destination
placeholders.description: Folder to copy into (created if missing)

syntaxParts.meaning: Copy subdirectories, including empty ones.

details.expectedOutput: A header, per-file lines, then a summary table of directories, files and bytes copied, skipped or failed.
sideEffects: Overwrites destination files that differ from the source.
cautions: Exit codes 0–7 mean success or partial success. 8 or higher means some copies failed.

commands.name: Delete a file
commands.summary: Permanently deletes a file. It does not go to the Recycle Bin.

placeholders.name: File
placeholders.description: Path of the file to delete (wildcards allowed)

sideEffects: The file is removed immediately and does not go to the Recycle Bin.
cautions: Wildcards like *.* can match far more files than intended.

commands.name: Delete a folder and its contents
commands.summary: Removes a folder with everything inside it, without asking for confirmation.

syntaxParts.meaning: Delete the folder, all files and all subfolders.
Quiet: don't ask for confirmation.

sideEffects: Everything under the folder is deleted permanently, not moved to the Recycle Bin.
cautions: Double-check the folder path. CommandDeck will treat critical targets (drive roots, Windows, your profile) as high impact.

commands.name: Find where a program is installed
commands.summary: Shows the full path of a program that runs when you type its name.
tasks: which version of a program runs

placeholders.name: Program
placeholders.description: Program name, e.g. git or python

details.expectedOutput: One path per match in PATH order, or "INFO: Could not find files for the given pattern(s)."

commands.name: Show system information
commands.summary: Windows version, install date, boot time, memory, installed updates and network cards.
tasks: what version of windows do i have
how much ram do i have
when did the pc last restart

details.expectedOutput: A list of labeled properties: OS Name, OS Version, System Boot Time, Total Physical Memory, Hotfix(s) and more.
cautions: Can take several seconds while it gathers data.

commands.name: Show my user, groups and privileges
commands.summary: Shows the current account, its security groups (including whether it is an administrator) and its privileges.

syntaxParts.meaning: User, SID, groups and privileges of the current access token.

details.expectedOutput: Sections: USER INFORMATION, GROUP INFORMATION, PRIVILEGES INFORMATION. A "High Mandatory Level" label means the window is elevated.

commands.name: List running processes
commands.summary: Shows running programs with their process ID and memory use.

details.expectedOutput: Columns: Image Name, PID, Session Name, Session#, Mem Usage.

commands.name: Force-close a program
commands.summary: Ends every process with the given program name, even if it is not responding.

syntaxParts.meaning: Select processes by image (file) name.
Force termination.

sideEffects: Unsaved work in that program is lost.
cautions: Ends every instance with that name.
Processes owned by other users or SYSTEM need administrator rights.

commands.name: Scan and repair system files
commands.summary: Checks protected Windows system files and replaces corrupted ones from a cached copy.

details.whenToUse: Windows behaves oddly or crashes and you suspect damaged system files.
details.expectedOutput: A progress percentage, then one of: no integrity violations found, corrupt files found and repaired, or corrupt files found that could not be repaired.
cautions: Takes several minutes.
If it cannot repair files, run DISM /RestoreHealth first and then sfc again.

commands.name: Repair the Windows image
commands.summary: Repairs the Windows component store, using Windows Update as the source, so system repairs can succeed.

syntaxParts.meaning: Act on the running Windows installation.
Scan for corruption and repair it.

details.expectedOutput: A progress bar, then "The restore operation completed successfully."
sideEffects: May download repair files from Windows Update.
cautions: Can take 10–30 minutes and may appear stuck at 20% or 62%. That is normal.

commands.name: Check a drive for errors (read-only)
commands.summary: Scans a drive's file system and reports problems without fixing anything.

syntaxParts.meaning: The drive to check. Without /f, chkdsk only reports.

details.expectedOutput: Stage-by-stage progress, then "Windows has scanned the file system and found no problems" or a list of issues.
cautions: Fixing errors needs chkdsk /f, which may require a restart for the system drive.

commands.name: Restart the computer now
commands.summary: Restarts Windows immediately, with no countdown.

syntaxParts.meaning: Restart after shutting down.
Wait 0 seconds before acting.

sideEffects: All programs close. Unsaved work may be lost.

commands.name: Show free space on a drive
commands.summary: Reports total, free and available bytes on a volume.
tasks: how much disk space is left

details.expectedOutput: Total free bytes, total bytes and total quota-free bytes for the volume.
cautions: Requires administrator rights. A standard user gets "Error 5: Access is denied". Without admin, use PowerShell Get-Volume instead.

commands.name: Format a drive
commands.summary: Erases a volume and creates a new NTFS file system on it (quick format).

placeholders.name: Drive
placeholders.description: Drive letter to format, e.g. E

syntaxParts.meaning: Create an NTFS file system.
Quick format: skip the full surface scan.

sideEffects: Every file on the volume becomes inaccessible.
cautions: Irreversible for practical purposes. Double-check the drive letter.
Windows refuses to format the drive it is running from.

commands.name: List local user accounts
commands.summary: Shows the user accounts that exist on this computer.

details.expectedOutput: A table of account names, then "The command completed successfully."

commands.name: List administrators
commands.summary: Shows which accounts belong to the local Administrators group.

details.expectedOutput: Alias name, comment, then the member list.

commands.name: List running services
commands.summary: Shows active Windows services with their state.

details.expectedOutput: One block per running service: SERVICE_NAME, DISPLAY_NAME, TYPE, STATE.
cautions: In PowerShell, sc is an alias for Set-Content. Type sc.exe there instead.

commands.name: Stop a service
commands.summary: Stops a running Windows service by name.

placeholders.name: ServiceName
placeholders.description: Service name or display name, e.g. Spooler

sideEffects: Features depending on the service stop working until it is started again.
cautions: Dependent services may be stopped too. net asks before stopping them.

commands.name: Show firewall status
commands.summary: Shows whether Windows Firewall is on for the domain, private and public profiles, and their settings.

details.expectedOutput: For each profile: State ON/OFF, firewall policy, logging settings.

commands.name: Show BitLocker status
commands.summary: Reports whether each drive is encrypted with BitLocker and how protection is configured.

details.expectedOutput: Per volume: size, conversion status, percentage encrypted, protection status, key protectors.
cautions: Requires administrator rights. A standard user gets an access-denied error.

commands.name: List environment variables
commands.summary: Shows every environment variable in the current session and its value.

details.expectedOutput: One NAME=value line per variable.

commands.name: Show the PATH variable
commands.summary: Prints the folders Windows searches when you type a program name.
tasks: why is a program not found

syntaxParts.meaning: CMD expands %NAME% to the variable's value.

details.expectedOutput: One long line of folders separated by semicolons.

commands.name: Set a permanent user variable
commands.summary: Creates or changes an environment variable for your account that persists across sessions.

sideEffects: Writes to your user environment in the registry.
cautions: Only new windows see the change, not the current one.
Values longer than 1024 characters are truncated. Never use setx to modify PATH from %PATH%.
